composition.serve_who: This sheet ("GENERATOR E-STOP", GMMS 108'-118) documents the wiring for the Emergency Stop signal path that trips PORT and STBD generators. All labels on the sheet (T/S M terminals feeding Re27 relay and PORT/STBD GEN E-STOP contacts, T/S C terminals 127/128/129 named PORT GEN SIGNAL / STBD GEN SIGNAL, and terminal 136 named EMERGENCY STOP) point to one function: the vessel's centralized Emergency Stop system commanding both generators to shut down. This matches the register's 654-emergency-stops node (Emergency Stops, logical 654) and is consistent with the established fact that 654-emergency-stops is fed from Q17 6A on the Emergency Panel (a different sheet). No other equipment is named on this sheet — generators themselves (610-generators) are the downstream targets referenced via cross-reference only, not detailed here.

equipment_groups.placement_reasoning: Sheet title is 'GENERATOR E-STOP'; terminal 136 is explicitly labeled EMERGENCY STOP with a normally-closed contact; the loop drives 'to PORT GEN E-STOP' and 'to STBD GEN E-STOP' outputs. This is the emergency-stop signal distribution for the generators, matching the register's Emergency Stops node (654-emergency-stops), which per established facts is fed from breaker Q17 6A on the Emergency Panel (a different, already-ingested sheet).

functions.label: Generator emergency-stop relay loop (Re27)
functions.sheet_region: center of sheet — Re27 relay (~0.44-0.55, 0.19-0.29) and its contact outputs; T/S M terminal strip (~0.26-0.31, 0.29-0.37); T/S C terminal strip (~0.61-0.72, 0.27-0.40)
functions.what_it_does: Provides the wired path by which an incoming emergency-stop command (arriving via T/S M from cable MU15-7, cross-referenced to DWG 110c) energises relay Re27, whose contacts break/route the E-STOP signal out to both the PORT and STBD generator E-STOP inputs. A separate normally-closed contact (terminal 136, labelled EMERGENCY STOP) sits in the T/S C block feeding the same signal chain, with PORT GEN SIGNAL (127) and STBD GEN SIGNAL (128) taps continuing to DWG 116 for further handling downstream.

flow_scenarios.path: MU15-7 multicore (see DWG 110c) -> T/S M pins 1,3,4 -> Re27 coil left-side contact group -> Re27 relay de-energised, contacts in rest position -> 'to PORT GEN E-STOP' and 'to STBD GEN E-STOP' lines held in run-permissive state -> T/S C terminals 127 (PORT GEN SIGNAL) and 128 (STBD GEN SIGNAL) pass status onward via cross-reference to DWG 116; terminal 136 (EMERGENCY STOP, normally-closed contact) remains closed, keeping the loop intact.

Command arrives at T/S M (from MU15-7 / DWG 110c) on pins 1/3/4 -> energises Re27 relay coil -> Re27 contacts switch -> upper contact output drives 'to PORT GEN E-STOP', lower contact output drives 'to STBD GEN E-STOP' -> both generators receive their E-STOP trip signal; simultaneously T/S C terminal 136 (EMERGENCY STOP NC contact) opens, breaking the signal path back through 127/128/129 toward DWG 116, registering the emergency condition upstream.

key_components: Relay Re27 — coil + dry contact pair driving PORT/STBD generator E-stop lines
Normally-closed contact 136 (EMERGENCY STOP) — breaks the loop when tripped
Terminal strip T/S M (8-way) — incoming command terminals 1-8, pins 7/8 linked by a dot (bridged)
Terminal strip T/S C — signal terminals 127 (PORT GEN SIGNAL), 128 (STBD GEN SIGNAL), 129, and 136 (EMERGENCY STOP)
functions.dry_data: Relay Re27, dry contact pair; terminal strips T/S M (8-way) and T/S C (127/128/129/136); no breaker/fuse shown on this sheet.

cross_references.what: Incoming cable MU15-7 into T/S M pin 1 (and related pins) — source of the E-stop command signal
PORT GEN SIGNAL (127), STBD GEN SIGNAL (128), and terminal 129 continuing onward from T/S C
PORT and STBD generator E-STOP inputs (physical generator-side termination of the 'to PORT GEN E-STOP' / 'to STBD GEN E-STOP' outputs)
